title: Gravity & Weight
subtitle: The pull that never lets go.

sections.title: What is gravity?
sections.body:
Gravity is a force that pulls every object towards every other object.

You only notice it near something huge. The Earth is huge, so it pulls you, your bag and a falling apple straight down towards its centre. Gravity never switches off and never needs to touch you to work.
sections.bodyEs: La gravedad es una fuerza que atrae cada objeto hacia todos los demás objetos. Solo la notas cerca de algo enorme. La Tierra es enorme, así que te atrae a ti, a tu mochila y a una manzana que cae, directamente hacia su centro. La gravedad nunca se apaga y no necesita tocarte para actuar.

sections.title: Mass is not weight
sections.titleEs: La masa no es el peso
sections.body:
Mass is how much stuff an object is made of. It is measured in kilograms and it never changes.

Weight is the pull of gravity on that mass. It is a force, so it is measured in newtons. Change the gravity and the weight changes, even though the mass has not.
sections.bodyEs: La masa es la cantidad de materia de la que está hecho un objeto. Se mide en kilogramos y nunca cambia. El peso es el tirón de la gravedad sobre esa masa. Es una fuerza, así que se mide en newtons. Si cambia la gravedad, cambia el peso, aunque la masa siga siendo la misma.

sections.title: Weight changes with the planet
sections.titleEs: El peso cambia según el planeta
sections.body:
Every world pulls with its own strength. On Earth gravity pulls with about 10 newtons for every kilogram.

The Moon is much smaller, so it pulls about six times more weakly. Jupiter is enormous and pulls far harder. Same astronaut, same mass, very different weight.
sections.bodyEs: Cada mundo tira con su propia fuerza. En la Tierra la gravedad tira con unos diez newtons por cada kilogramo. La Luna es mucho más pequeña, así que tira unas seis veces más débil. Júpiter es enorme y tira mucho más fuerte. El mismo astronauta, la misma masa, un peso muy distinto.

sections.title: Everything falls together
sections.body:
Drop a hammer and a feather and the hammer wins — but not because it is heavier.

The feather loses because air pushes back on it. Take the air away and both hit the ground at exactly the same moment. Astronauts have actually tried this on the Moon.
sections.bodyEs: Si sueltas un martillo y una pluma, gana el martillo, pero no porque pese más. La pluma pierde porque el aire la empuja hacia atrás. Si quitas el aire, los dos llegan al suelo exactamente al mismo tiempo. Los astronautas lo han probado de verdad en la Luna.

keyPoints: Gravity pulls everything towards the centre of the Earth.
Mass is measured in kilograms and never changes.
Weight is a force, measured in newtons.
Weight = mass multiplied by the strength of gravity.
Without air, heavy and light objects fall together.
keyPointsEs: La gravedad atrae todo hacia el centro de la Tierra.
La masa se mide en kilogramos y nunca cambia.
El peso es una fuerza que se mide en newtons.
Peso = masa multiplicada por la intensidad de la gravedad.
Sin aire, los objetos pesados y ligeros caen al mismo tiempo.

glossary.definitionEn: The force pulling objects towards each other.
glossary.definitionEs: La fuerza que atrae los objetos unos hacia otros.

glossary.definitionEn: How much matter an object contains, in kilograms.
glossary.definitionEs: La cantidad de materia que contiene un objeto, en kilogramos.

glossary.definitionEn: The force of gravity on a mass, in newtons.
glossary.definitionEs: La fuerza de la gravedad sobre una masa, en newtons.

glossary.definitionEn: Falling with gravity as the only force acting.
glossary.definitionEs: Caer cuando la gravedad es la única fuerza que actúa.

questions.prompt: Which of these never changes when you travel to the Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter in you and it never changes. Weight is the pull of gravity, so it drops on the Moon.
Weight is a force, and forces are measured in newtons. Kilograms measure mass instead.

questions.prompt: On the Moon a hammer and a feather are dropped together. They...
questions.explanation: The Moon has no air, so nothing slows the feather down. With only gravity acting, everything falls together.

questions.prompt: Your mass stays the same, but your ___ changes on another planet.
questions.explanation: Your mass is the same everywhere, but weight depends on the strength of gravity where you are standing.

questions.prompt: Three of these are measured in newtons. Which one is not?
questions.explanation: Weight, air resistance and friction are all forces, so all are measured in newtons. Mass is measured in kilograms.

questions.prompt: Match each quantity to its unit or meaning.
questions.explanation: Mass and weight sound alike but use different units, and free fall means gravity is the only force acting.
